description: The plot titled “BBQ” shows accuracy values for several model variants as the number of demonstrations increases, allowing their performance trends to be viewed on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “#Demonstrations,” uses a linear scale, spans from 0 to 1500, and shows regularly spaced tick labels every 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and displays tick labels at 45, 50, and 55 (a 5-unit interval), with the plotted values extending slightly above 55. The Squared-Exponential series is drawn as a dark navy solid line with circular markers; it begins near 52 at 0 demonstrations, rises to about 56 by around 250 demonstrations, and then remains roughly flat near 56 through 1500 demonstrations with only small fluctuations. The Tanh series is a medium-blue solid line with circular markers; it starts around 48 at 0 demonstrations and stays close to 48 across the range, ending near 47–48 at 1500 demonstrations. The ELU series is a light gray-blue solid line with circular markers; it begins around 46 at 0 demonstrations and remains near 46–47 for most of the x-range, ending around 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B reference is shown as a pink dashed horizontal line (no markers) positioned near 43 accuracy and remains constant across all demonstration counts.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations, providing a comparison of performance trends on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 and tick labels at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', with a linear scale ranging from 45 to 55, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, increases steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes. The 'Tanh' model begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points, performing significantly worse than the other models. The 'Squared Exponential' model consistently outperforms all other models, with the 'ELU' model showing the second-best performance overall.
